pages.title: How to use this book
pages.part: Getting started

elements.text: How to use this book

This handbook is organized for two kinds of reading. Read Parts I–V from the start to understand the product, architecture, data and analysis. Use Part VI as an operational cookbook when a concrete failure occurs. Each case begins with an observable symptom and ends with a verification condition and a boundary that prevents an unsafe shortcut.

Status language is deliberate. “Implemented” means code exists. “Verified” means an identified test or live check passed. “Enabled” means a recurring process is active on this laptop. “Pending” means a required proof, permission or setup step remains. A written Phase specification is a target, not proof that the feature is in production.

Use the current-state table before relying on any workflow. Use each module section to locate source files, commands, inputs and outputs. For incidents, first preserve the original evidence and identify the affected layer; then perform the smallest reversible repair and verify it in the database or dashboard. Record significant operating changes in Git with a clear commit message.

Never copy actual credentials into this document. Keep the local environment file private. Market analysis, model output and historical statistics are not trading instructions. The system makes no claim of predictive accuracy or positive investment edge.

pages.title: Executive summary
pages.part: Getting started

elements.text: Executive summary

Fin Analysis is a personal, single-owner research application for Indian equities. Its data and calculations flow through independent Python modules and a Supabase Postgres hub. A local Next.js dashboard presents charts, signals, news, event studies, backtests, evidence-linked discussions, operation records and alerts. It does not submit, alter or cancel orders.

The repository has progressed through five specifications. The first four implemented the database, ingestion, logbook, signals, backtests, news analysis, Gemini-based research workflows and protected dashboard features. Phase 5 adds scheduling infrastructure and operations tooling. Some important Phase 5 acceptance work remains incomplete, so the project must not be represented as fully commissioned.

Three laptop services are currently active: a daily database backup at 20:30 IST, alert checks every 15 minutes, and personal RSS news updates every 30 minutes. News updates currently poll Mint and Economic Times. Their latest successful initial poll added 84 items; all 84 passed deduplication and sentiment processing. The news task does not refresh stock prices.

The live alert checker completed 34 checks without group failures after a recent repair; its latest reported run has six unresolved stale-price warnings. Telegram delivery is enabled after a successful test. A warning waits through 22:00–07:00 IST; a critical alert bypasses quiet hours. The main market/research scheduler remains disabled, as do automated price collection, exchange announcement polling and browser sources.

A recent database backup was copied to a local directory and a Google Drive Desktop synced folder. Online presence was manually verified. A two-table restore smoke test matched 4,482 candle rows and six watchlist rows. That is not a full Supabase recovery drill. Retention deletion is not enabled. Human review of the 100-item news accuracy sample remains pending, and no model accuracy or investment edge is claimed.

elements.text: System flow

At a healthy, commissioned state, an approved source supplies observations. Ingestion validates them against expected sessions and symbol contracts, then stores raw records with dates, provenance and adjustments. Signals derive versioned values from a declared price basis. News collection stores bounded publisher feed content, links companies, deduplicates, classifies events and computes local scores. Research agents consume evidence frozen at a cutoff and return structured claims. Backtests evaluate explicit historical assumptions. The dashboard reads these results and exposes protected owner workflows. The logbook and health tables preserve what happened.

Observe alerts, task state, retries, backups and measured recovery evidence.

elements.text: Material owner choices

The owner chose a private Telegram chat for alerts and a private Google Drive Desktop directory for the secondary backup. The owner approved two 0.5 bonus adjustment factors after price comparisons. The user explicitly deferred human labelling of the gold news set. Gemini was selected for Phase 4; an earlier API key was disclosed in chat and rotation remains a security maintenance item.
What must not be inferred

A configured CLI is not the same as a scheduled pipeline. A recurring health checker does not fetch prices. A current local RSS task does not imply exchange announcements are fetched. A model verifier is not independent truth review. A successful checksum is not an online cloud receipt. A limited table restore does not demonstrate full recovery. A generated historical metric does not show a live edge.

pages.title: Part 01  Project purpose and operating boundaries
pages.part: Part 01  Project purpose and operating boundaries

elements.text: Part 01  Project purpose and operating boundaries

The repository builds a single-owner, local-first research tool for Indian equities. It collects permitted data, calculates indicators, evaluates historical rules, and presents evidence with its provenance. It never places orders. Treat every analytical output as research, not advice.
Primary references: README.md; PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md; WORKINGS.md.
Operating invariant: The current implementation and verification records define what is running. Phase documents describe desired scope and may predate later source reviews.

Start by identifying the relevant source-of-truth file and the last verified state. Distinguish configuration in the repository from runtime configuration in the hosted database and ignored local environment. Prefer read-only inspection before any repair. Preserve raw input and logbook context; derived output can then be reproduced and compared.

A useful handoff records the timestamp in IST and UTC when relevant, module and run ID, source or symbol, exact task status, observed output, intended repair, result, and any remaining caveat. Do not include secret values, personal prompt text or unnecessary article content. If the evidence is incomplete, record that uncertainty instead of guessing.
How this part is organized

The following ten cases use the same incident format so an operator can scan quickly: trigger, interpretation, diagnostic path, safe response, proof of recovery and a limit on what the result establishes. The section is operational documentation, not authorization to enable a source or expand the project’s intended use.
Reference checklist

rows: Find the module README, current config and migration contract.
Read recent logbook entries, health rows, scheduled-task result and relevant database records.
Use the lowest-risk reversible action; retain raw and prior-run provenance.
Run the specific unit or live check and inspect its observable output.
Record what recovered, what did not, and who or what still must act.

pages.title: 01.01  Purpose conflicts
pages.part: Part 01  Project purpose and operating boundaries

elements.text: 01.01  Purpose conflicts

This case begins when an operator observes “purpose conflicts” in the relevant module or workflow. Treat that observation as a symptom, not yet a confirmed root cause. Establish the affected symbol, source, run identity and timestamp before changing state.

First inspect README.md; PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md; WORKINGS.md. Compare the active repository configuration with the database row and the latest agent_events/health_checks evidence. Check whether the expected trigger actually ran, whether a dependency or permission gate intentionally skipped it, and whether the same input already has a successful idempotent result. Preserve the failing attempt and its source metadata.

The safe response is to correct the source or configuration at the layer that owns the fault, then rerun only the failed unit where possible. Keep raw rows and approved historical decisions intact. A 403, access refusal, unreviewed source, unsupported database change or missing approval is a stop condition, not a reason to retry repeatedly or bypass a guard. A network outage calls for a bounded retry after recovery; a semantic or permission error requires review first.
Case-specific action: Keep the personal, read-only scope; place any order-related capability out of scope.

Close the case only after a concrete check passes: expected records or a clear skip are visible, the run exits successfully, there are no new failed groups, checksums or input hashes match when relevant, and the dashboard reflects the stored result. Confirm whether an incident auto-resolved and whether a recovery notification was eligible. Record the evidence and residual limitation in the logbook/runbook.

elements.text: Part 02  System architecture and module contracts

Python services are independent processes joined through Postgres tables. The Next.js dashboard uses the public client for permitted reads and authenticated server routes for restricted actions. The database is the integration boundary. Shared code is kept small.
Primary references: ARCHITECTURE.md; db/migrations/; shared/.

pages.title: Part 03  Data model and Supabase operations
pages.part: Part 03  Data model and Supabase operations

elements.text: Part 03  Data model and Supabase operations

Supabase Postgres is the hosted state store. Migrations define watchlist, candles, signals, articles, research, queue and operations data. RLS restricts table access; server-side service credentials never belong in the browser.
Primary references: db/README.md; db/migrations/001_init.sql through 010_alert_operations.sql.

Operating invariant: Run migrations in numeric order against an explicitly selected project. Review RLS, grants, functions and advisors for every schema change. Backups are separate from hosted provider retention.

Start by identifying the relevant source-of-truth file and the last verified state. Distinguish configuration in the repository from runtime configuration in the hosted database and ignored local environment. Prefer read-only inspection before any repair. Preserve raw input and logbook context; derived output can then be reproduced and compared.

A useful handoff records the timestamp in IST and UTC when relevant, module and run ID, source or symbol, exact task status, observed output, intended repair, result, and any remaining caveat. Do not include secret values, personal prompt text or unnecessary article content. If the evidence is incomplete, record that uncertainty instead of guessing.
How this part is organized

The following ten cases use the same incident format so an operator can scan quickly: trigger, interpretation, diagnostic path, safe response, proof of recovery and a limit on what the result establishes. The section is operational documentation, not authorization to enable a source or expand the project’s intended use.

pages.title: Part 04  Local setup and Python environments
pages.part: Part 04  Local setup and Python environments

elements.text: Part 04  Local setup and Python environments

Each module has its own locked dependencies because numerical, machine-learning and web packages differ. The Windows scheduled tasks must use Python paths the interactive Windows user can actually read.
Primary references: README.md; requirements-lock.txt; */requirements-lock.txt; ops/.

Operating invariant: Install from committed locks. Do not combine module environments to resolve conflicts. A green import test in one environment does not prove another scheduled environment can run.

Start by identifying the relevant source-of-truth file and the last verified state. Distinguish configuration in the repository from runtime configuration in the hosted database and ignored local environment. Prefer read-only inspection before any repair. Preserve raw input and logbook context; derived output can then be reproduced and compared.

A useful handoff records the timestamp in IST and UTC when relevant, module and run ID, source or symbol, exact task status, observed output, intended repair, result, and any remaining caveat. Do not include secret values, personal prompt text or unnecessary article content. If the evidence is incomplete, record that uncertainty instead of guessing.
How this part is organized

The following ten cases use the same incident format so an operator can scan quickly: trigger, interpretation, diagnostic path, safe response, proof of recovery and a limit on what the result establishes. The section is operational documentation, not authorization to enable a source or expand the project’s intended use.
Reference checklist

rows: Find the module README, current config and migration contract.
Read recent logbook entries, health rows, scheduled-task result and relevant database records.
Use the lowest-risk reversible action; retain raw and prior-run provenance.
Run the specific unit or live check and inspect its observable output.
Record what recovered, what did not, and who or what still must act.

pages.part: Part 07  Candles validation and source failure

elements.text: Part 07  Candles validation and source failure
Ingestion is designed to read active symbols, fetch daily OHLCV, validate rows, preserve source and adjustment metadata, and write idempotently. Price scheduling is currently not commissioned.
Primary references: ingest/README.md; ingest/main.py; ingest/validate.py; config/ingest.yaml.

Operating invariant: A local historical dataset exists, but current-session freshness requires a working approved provider and active schedule. A missing price is not repaired by rerunning a signal calculator.

Start by identifying the relevant source-of-truth file and the last verified state. Distinguish configuration in the repository from runtime configuration in the hosted database and ignored local environment. Prefer read-only inspection before any repair. Preserve raw input and logbook context; derived output can then be reproduced and compared.

A useful handoff records the timestamp in IST and UTC when relevant, module and run ID, source or symbol, exact task status, observed output, intended repair, result, and any remaining caveat. Do not include secret values, personal prompt text or unnecessary article content. If the evidence is incomplete, record that uncertainty instead of guessing.
How this part is organized

The following ten cases use the same incident format so an operator can scan quickly: trigger, interpretation, diagnostic path, safe response, proof of recovery and a limit on what the result establishes. The section is operational documentation, not authorization to enable a source or expand the project’s intended use.
Reference checklist

rows: Find the module README, current config and migration contract.
Read recent logbook entries, health rows, scheduled-task result and relevant database records.
Use the lowest-risk reversible action; retain raw and prior-run provenance.
Run the specific unit or live check and inspect its observable output.
Record what recovered, what did not, and who or what still must act.

pages.part: Part 08  Trading calendar actions and price basis

elements.text: Part 08  Trading calendar actions and price basis
The calendar distinguishes exchange sessions from holidays. Human-approved corporate-action factors feed an adjusted view; raw candles stay immutable. Signals and tests record the basis they use.
Primary references: config/calendar.yaml; db/migrations/009_calendar_adjust.sql; dashboard/app/corporate-actions/.
Operating invariant: Two reviewed bonus factors are approved: RELIANCE on 2024-10-28 and HDFCBANK on 2025-08-26, both 0.5. A proposal, parsed announcement or guessed ratio is not an approval.

Start by identifying the relevant source-of-truth file and the last verified state. Distinguish configuration in the repository from runtime configuration in the hosted database and ignored local environment. Prefer read-only inspection before any repair. Preserve raw input and logbook context; derived output can then be reproduced and compared.

A useful handoff records the timestamp in IST and UTC when relevant, module and run ID, source or symbol, exact task status, observed output, intended repair, result, and any remaining caveat. Do not include secret values, personal prompt text or unnecessary article content. If the evidence is incomplete, record that uncertainty instead of guessing.
How this part is organized

The following ten cases use the same incident format so an operator can scan quickly: trigger, interpretation, diagnostic path, safe response, proof of recovery and a limit on what the result establishes. The section is operational documentation, not authorization to enable a source or expand the project’s intended use.

pages.title: Part 11  News feeds and local processing
pages.part: Part 11  News feeds and local processing

elements.text: Part 11  News feeds and local processing

The live news task polls two enabled personal RSS sources, stores publisher-supplied titles/snippets and links, then performs deduplication, entity linking, event classification, local sentiment and embeddings.
Primary references: news/README.md; config/feeds.yaml; config/news.yaml; news/main.py.

Operating invariant: Mint and Economic Times are enabled for this private reader. Business Standard, The Hindu, Moneycontrol and exchange announcements remain disabled for the reasons recorded in docs/SOURCES_TERMS.md. No full articles are collected.

Start by identifying the relevant source-of-truth file and the last verified state. Distinguish configuration in the repository from runtime configuration in the hosted database and ignored local environment. Prefer read-only inspection before any repair. Preserve raw input and logbook context; derived output can then be reproduced and compared.

A useful handoff records the timestamp in IST and UTC when relevant, module and run ID, source or symbol, exact task status, observed output, intended repair, result, and any remaining caveat. Do not include secret values, personal prompt text or unnecessary article content. If the evidence is incomplete, record that uncertainty instead of guessing.
How this part is organized

The following ten cases use the same incident format so an operator can scan quickly: trigger, interpretation, diagnostic path, safe response, proof of recovery and a limit on what the result establishes. The section is operational documentation, not authorization to enable a source or expand the project’s intended use.
Reference checklist

rows: Find the module README, current config and migration contract.
Read recent logbook entries, health rows, scheduled-task result and relevant database records.
Use the lowest-risk reversible action; retain raw and prior-run provenance.
Run the specific unit or live check and inspect its observable output.
Record what recovered, what did not, and who or what still must act.

pages.title: Part 14  Queue scheduling and process control
pages.part: Part 14  Queue scheduling and process control

elements.text: Part 14  Queue scheduling and process control

Phase 5 includes a dependency queue, leases, attempts, retries, worker ownership, cancellation and heartbeat controls. Market/research pipelines stay disabled until their source and commissioning gates pass.
Primary references: scheduler/README.md; scheduler/; config/schedule.yaml; config/modules.yaml.
Operating invariant: The backup, alert and RSS Windows tasks are independent. The main scheduler heartbeat is intentionally paused when every market/research pipeline is disabled.

Start by identifying the relevant source-of-truth file and the last verified state. Distinguish configuration in the repository from runtime configuration in the hosted database and ignored local environment. Prefer read-only inspection before any repair. Preserve raw input and logbook context; derived output can then be reproduced and compared.

A useful handoff records the timestamp in IST and UTC when relevant, module and run ID, source or symbol, exact task status, observed output, intended repair, result, and any remaining caveat. Do not include secret values, personal prompt text or unnecessary article content. If the evidence is incomplete, record that uncertainty instead of guessing.
How this part is organized

The following ten cases use the same incident format so an operator can scan quickly: trigger, interpretation, diagnostic path, safe response, proof of recovery and a limit on what the result establishes. The section is operational documentation, not authorization to enable a source or expand the project’s intended use.
Reference checklist

rows: Find the module README, current config and migration contract.
Read recent logbook entries, health rows, scheduled-task result and relevant database records.
Use the lowest-risk reversible action; retain raw and prior-run provenance.
Run the specific unit or live check and inspect its observable output.
Record what recovered, what did not, and who or what still must act.

pages.title: Part 15  Alerts and Telegram delivery
pages.part: Part 15  Alerts and Telegram delivery

elements.text: Part 15  Alerts and Telegram delivery
A separate health task checks the database every 15 minutes, records deduplicated incidents, resolves recovered ones and can send bounded private Telegram batches.
Primary references: alerts/README.md; alerts/checks.py; alerts/main.py; config/alerts.yaml.

Operating invariant: Telegram test delivery succeeded and notification delivery is enabled. Warning quiet hours are 22:00-07:00 IST; critical alerts bypass quiet hours. A powered-off laptop cannot monitor itself.

Start by identifying the relevant source-of-truth file and the last verified state. Distinguish configuration in the repository from runtime configuration in the hosted database and ignored local environment. Prefer read-only inspection before any repair. Preserve raw input and logbook context; derived output can then be reproduced and compared.

A useful handoff records the timestamp in IST and UTC when relevant, module and run ID, source or symbol, exact task status, observed output, intended repair, result, and any remaining caveat. Do not include secret values, personal prompt text or unnecessary article content. If the evidence is incomplete, record that uncertainty instead of guessing.
How this part is organized

The following ten cases use the same incident format so an operator can scan quickly: trigger, interpretation, diagnostic path, safe response, proof of recovery and a limit on what the result establishes. The section is operational documentation, not authorization to enable a source or expand the project’s intended use.
Reference checklist

rows: Find the module README, current config and migration contract.
Read recent logbook entries, health rows, scheduled-task result and relevant database records.
Use the lowest-risk reversible action; retain raw and prior-run provenance.
Run the specific unit or live check and inspect its observable output.
Record what recovered, what did not, and who or what still must act.

elements.text: Part 16  Backup restoration and retention
A separate Windows task runs a PostgreSQL custom-format dump daily, verifies archive contents and hashes, exports non-secret configuration, and copies it to local and Google Drive-synced folders.

Operating invariant: Full restore readiness is not established. A two-table smoke test matched 4,482 candles and six watchlist rows. Cloud presence was manually observed; machine-readable manifest flags remain appropriately false.

Start by identifying the relevant source-of-truth file and the last verified state. Distinguish configuration in the repository from runtime configuration in the hosted database and ignored local environment. Prefer read-only inspection before any repair. Preserve raw input and logbook context; derived output can then be reproduced and compared.

A useful handoff records the timestamp in IST and UTC when relevant, module and run ID, source or symbol, exact task status, observed output, intended repair, result, and any remaining caveat. Do not include secret values, personal prompt text or unnecessary article content. If the evidence is incomplete, record that uncertainty instead of guessing.

pages.title: Part 18  Verification tests and CI
pages.part: Part 18  Verification tests and CI

elements.text: Part 18  Verification tests and CI

Module tests cover arithmetic, state transitions, source failures, browser security, provider adapters and UI behavior. GitHub Actions validates submitted code without real secrets or live provider calls.
Primary references: docs/VERIFICATION.md; docs/PHASE_2_VERIFICATION.md; docs/PHASE_3_VERIFICATION.md; .github/workflows/.
Operating invariant: A test proves only the condition it exercises. Separate offline fixtures, SQL contract drills, current live-system checks and owner review in status reporting.

Start by identifying the relevant source-of-truth file and the last verified state. Distinguish configuration in the repository from runtime configuration in the hosted database and ignored local environment. Prefer read-only inspection before any repair. Preserve raw input and logbook context; derived output can then be reproduced and compared.

A useful handoff records the timestamp in IST and UTC when relevant, module and run ID, source or symbol, exact task status, observed output, intended repair, result, and any remaining caveat. Do not include secret values, personal prompt text or unnecessary article content. If the evidence is incomplete, record that uncertainty instead of guessing.
How this part is organized

The following ten cases use the same incident format so an operator can scan quickly: trigger, interpretation, diagnostic path, safe response, proof of recovery and a limit on what the result establishes. The section is operational documentation, not authorization to enable a source or expand the project’s intended use.
Reference checklist

rows: Find the module README, current config and migration contract.
Read recent logbook entries, health rows, scheduled-task result and relevant database records.
Use the lowest-risk reversible action; retain raw and prior-run provenance.
Run the specific unit or live check and inspect its observable output.
Record what recovered, what did not, and who or what still must act.

pages.title: Part 19  Runbooks incidents and recovery
pages.part: Part 19  Runbooks incidents and recovery

elements.text: Part 19  Runbooks incidents and recovery
Operations include scheduled tasks, incident triage, safe retries, environment troubleshooting, backup checks, restore preparation and controlled credential rotation.
Primary references: ops/RUNBOOK.md; alerts/README.md; scheduler/README.md.

Operating invariant: Prefer the smallest repair that preserves source evidence and past results. Check Task Scheduler state and result, logs, database and destination health before restarting or marking resolved.

Start by identifying the relevant source-of-truth file and the last verified state. Distinguish configuration in the repository from runtime configuration in the hosted database and ignored local environment. Prefer read-only inspection before any repair. Preserve raw input and logbook context; derived output can then be reproduced and compared.

A useful handoff records the timestamp in IST and UTC when relevant, module and run ID, source or symbol, exact task status, observed output, intended repair, result, and any remaining caveat. Do not include secret values, personal prompt text or unnecessary article content. If the evidence is incomplete, record that uncertainty instead of guessing.
How this part is organized

The following ten cases use the same incident format so an operator can scan quickly: trigger, interpretation, diagnostic path, safe response, proof of recovery and a limit on what the result establishes. The section is operational documentation, not authorization to enable a source or expand the project’s intended use.
Reference checklist

rows: Find the module README, current config and migration contract.
Read recent logbook entries, health rows, scheduled-task result and relevant database records.
Use the lowest-risk reversible action; retain raw and prior-run provenance.
Run the specific unit or live check and inspect its observable output.
Record what recovered, what did not, and who or what still must act.

elements.text: Part 20  Release governance and future acceptance
A change is complete after implementation, appropriate verification, clear status documentation, an understandable commit and the requested GitHub push. Phase 5 completion has further proofs.
Primary references: PHASE_1.md through PHASE_5.md; docs/PHASE_5_PROGRESS.md; .github/.

Operating invariant: Remaining gates include source-compliant price collection, broader operations views, full restore and five unattended trading days. Do not call the project or Phase 5 finished before those pass.

Start by identifying the relevant source-of-truth file and the last verified state. Distinguish configuration in the repository from runtime configuration in the hosted database and ignored local environment. Prefer read-only inspection before any repair. Preserve raw input and logbook context; derived output can then be reproduced and compared.

A useful handoff records the timestamp in IST and UTC when relevant, module and run ID, source or symbol, exact task status, observed output, intended repair, result, and any remaining caveat. Do not include secret values, personal prompt text or unnecessary article content. If the evidence is incomplete, record that uncertainty instead of guessing.
How this part is organized

The following ten cases use the same incident format so an operator can scan quickly: trigger, interpretation, diagnostic path, safe response, proof of recovery and a limit on what the result establishes. The section is operational documentation, not authorization to enable a source or expand the project’s intended use.
Reference checklist

rows: Find the module README, current config and migration contract.
Read recent logbook entries, health rows, scheduled-task result and relevant database records.
Use the lowest-risk reversible action; retain raw and prior-run provenance.
Run the specific unit or live check and inspect its observable output.
Record what recovered, what did not, and who or what still must act.

elements.text: Appendix A  Daily opening routine

rows: Check dashboard login, latest candle timestamp, exchange calendar, source status and open incidents.
Inspect the task result and logbook. Confirm articles carry publication time/source and price rows use the expected basis.
Check signal input hash, report cutoff, evidence strength, unresolved claim counts and sample size.
Review stale data and alerts; let scheduled backup run. Verify both destinations when its task reports failure or Drive was offline.
Inspect disk/database capacity, source terms review dates, task runtimes, model quota and backup retention proposals without deleting anything.

elements.text: Appendix B  Safe commands
Open PowerShell from the repository root. Commands below use only local files and configured credentials; review the target before running writes. Never pass secrets as command arguments.
news/.venv/Scripts/python.exe news/main.py fetch
news/.venv/Scripts/python.exe news/main.py process
ops/alerts.ps1
ops/backup.ps1
scheduler/.venv/Scripts/python.exe scheduler/main.py status
news/.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest news/tests -q
signals/.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest signals/tests -q
backtest/.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest backtest/tests -q
npm run typecheck --prefix dashboard
git status --short
Appendix C  Source hierarchy and evidence

Use current migrations for schema; current config for intended toggles; code for actual behavior; live task and database evidence for operational state; verification records for precisely scoped historical checks; phase documents for requirements; vendor and publisher pages for current policy. Repository markdown can be stale. This handbook’s edition date does not turn a previously checked provider policy into a permanent approval.

For current source access, consult docs/SOURCES_TERMS.md before every proposed source change. For a decision about service limits, check the provider’s current documentation. Keep citations and terms-check dates in the source register rather than relying on memory.
Appendix D  Unfinished acceptance
A permitted daily price data source must be selected and exercised before price freshness alerts can be cleared reliably.
The entire Supabase project recovery workflow must be proven on an isolated target, including schema, roles, extensions, RLS, data, dashboard connectivity and restore timing.
Retention requires a reviewed dry run, exact table scopes, protected never-prune tables, a validated backup and a rollback plan before deletion implementation is enabled.
The full project must complete five unattended trading days with the prescribed failure drills before Phase 5 can be accepted.
The 100-item human news-label sample remains unreviewed; no accuracy claim is supported.
Gemini key rotation must be confirmed after the key was previously disclosed in chat.
Source access permissions and review dates must be checked before changing currently disabled feeds, price providers, exchange APIs or browser sources.
A future edition should update the operating state, scheduled task evidence, source register, provider policies, open acceptance items, and exact relevant Git revision before release.
